questions: ga1
BF₁₀ for baseline SBP between the randomised arms is 0.19. What does that mean?
Strong evidence that the arms differ at baseline
Moderate evidence for no baseline difference
The test failed because the arms are balanced
The p-value for the difference is 0.19
BF₁₀ = 0.19 means BF₀₁ ≈ 5.3: the data are about 5 times more likely under 'no difference', moderate evidence for the null.

What do the `grouped_*` functions do?
Merge several datasets before plotting them
Repeat the analysis within each level of a variable
Pool all groups into one overall comparison
Fit one mixed model with a random effect for each group
grouped_ggbetweenstats() and friends run the same plot and test separately in each level of grouping.var and combine the panels.

Your variables have outliers. Which `ggcorrmat()` type suits them?
`type = "parametric"`
`type = "robust"`
`type = "bayes"`
`type = "pearson"`
The robust option (percentage bend correlation) limits the influence of outliers.
qa1
Which citation syntax gives (Patil, 2021) in the text?
`@patil2021`
Square brackets put the citation in parentheses; a bare @key gives Patil (2021); -@ hides the author.

What does `shinylive` let you do in a Quarto page?
Host a Shiny app on shinyapps.io for free
Run a Shiny app in the browser, with no server
Convert a Shiny app into a static PNG image
Connect the page to a database server automatically
shinylive compiles the app to WebAssembly, so it runs in the reader's browser from a static page.

`bibliography:`
`cite-method:`
